transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-03-15
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Maya Cohen (Redwood AE), Liam Ortega (Redwood SE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE); Eli Navarro (CTO - Cairn), Samira Khan (Head of MLOps), Jon Park (Platform Engineer), Tanya Reed (Security)

Summary:
Cairn Labs is evaluating dedicated capacity from Redwood for productionizing their multimodal inference platform. Primary drivers: predictable tail latencies for user-facing apps, tenant isolation across teams, and burst capacity for batch re-runs. They are sensitive about data residency and KMS integration. They want a benchmark and cost model for reserved GPU pools and clarity on isolation/topology options.

Topics covered:
- Current infra and workload shape
- Isolation (single-tenant nodes vs soft multi-tenant fencing)
- Burst strategies and warm-pool heuristics
- Quantization and perf tradeoffs vs model fidelity
- Security: KMS, audit logs, SAML/SSO
- Next steps: pricing, benchmark plan, security docs

Action items listed above in metadata.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for jumping on. Quick roll call — we'll keep this to 45ish minutes and then capture next steps. Eli, Samira, Jon, Tanya, thanks for taking the time.
[00:12] Eli (Cairn): Yeah thanks, Maya. Super excited to chat. We ran your hosted trial last quarter, liked the latency, but at scale we're looking for reserved capacity; want to avoid noisy neighbor tail spikes.
[00:23] Liam (Redwood SE): Great, can you give us a quick picture of current traffic? p50, p95, burst patterns, and the models you plan to serve?
[00:35] Samira (Cairn): Sure. Main thing: user chat flows hitting a multimodal model — text + small images. Baseline is about 120 reqs/s average, p95 latency target is 250ms token streaming, we see 2x spikes during new feature releases and monthly batch reruns that can last 20-30 mins. We also have a background re-embed job that can flood GPUs.
[00:58] Jon (Cairn): Right now we run on a mix of preemptible nodes and some reserved instances in cloud, but we don't have fine-grained GPU isolation. We saw OOMs last month when the re-embed kicked off during a release.
[01:12] Priya (Redwood SE): Thanks — that helps. A couple clarifying Qs: are you looking for single-tenant physical nodes, or would isolating by tenant via soft fencing be acceptable? Also, any regulatory constraints on model traces or KV cache dumps?
[01:28] Tanya (Cairn Security): We need audit logs and customer-separated keys. All inference logs must be encrypted at rest with our KMS and we want the ability to rotate keys. SOC2 is table stakes.
[01:41] Maya (Redwood AE): Perfect — Redwood Private can do VPC + customer KMS; Dedicated offers reserved GPU pools with tenancy options. We can map this out, incuding warm pools for burst.
[01:51] Eli (Cairn): What's the difference practically between single-tenant nodes and a dedicated pool with tenant fencing? We care about deterministic latency.
[02:05] Liam (Redwood SE): Good question. Single-tenant nodes give you physical isolation — no co-located workloads — so jitter from other teams is eliminated. Tenant fencing (soft isolation) keeps workloads logically isolated on a shared pool, usually with cgroups/isolators and scheduling quotas; it reduces costs but may not guarantee absolute tail stability under extreme contention.
[02:30] Samira (Cairn): Cost will be a big factor. We need to model unit economics: per-token cost vs reserved monthly amortized cost. Any empirical numbers you can share?
[02:43] Maya (Redwood AE): We'll share a pricing sheet and a sample cost model. For the benchmark phase, we'll size reserved nodes based on your peak percentiles. We'll also show the impact of batching and KV cache hit rates on effective token cost.
[02:57] Jon (Cairn): Regarding burst, what are your warm-pool prewarm times? We can't have 30s cold starts for some user flows.
[03:07] Liam (Redwood SE): Warm-pool prewarm depends on model size and quantization. For a 30B model, a warm prewarmed GPU can join a pool in under 8s if persistent KV cache is used; cold starts from scratch are longer. We also offer hot-pools (kept warmed) for critical routes but those incur reserved costs.
[03:26] Tanya (Cairn): Do you support HSM-backed KMS or only cloud KMS integrations? We need FIPS and HSM for some keys.
[03:35] Priya (Redwood SE): Redwood supports customer-managed KMS integrations; for HSM-backed rotation we can work with your KMS provider. For on-prem/private deployments we can integrate with HSM appliances as required. We'll attach the compliance brief.
[03:49] Eli (Cairn): One of our weird constraints: we sometimes run large batch reruns that need all GPUs for 45 minutes. Can Redwood preempt user-facing traffic for batch jobs or do we need separate pools?
[04:02] Liam (Redwood SE): Two approaches — scheduled batch windows using dedicated batch pools, or burst to shared pools with prioritized routing. Preempting user traffic is risky for UX; better to carve out reserved capacity for user-facing service and use separate reserved burst pools or scheduled batch maintenance.
[04:19] Samira (Cairn): Makes sense. For throughput characterization, what telemetry do you provide per-token latency and per-route cost breakdowns?
[04:29] Maya (Redwood AE): Redwood Console gives per-route token breakdowns, p50/p95/p99 latencies, cost by model and route, and tracing hooks. We can also surface caching hit rates.
[04:40] Jon (Cairn): How do rollouts work if we pin a model version? Can we canary on a subset of nodes?
[04:48] Priya (Redwood SE): Yes — canary deploys across dedicated pools are supported. You can route a % of traffic to a canary node or run A/B tests and automatic fallback if errors or regressions occur.
[04:59] Eli (Cairn): A question on telemetry fidelity: we need raw request logs for debugging, but redacted for PII. Can we get both aggregated metrics and raw logs with token-level timestamps?
[05:13] Tanya (Cairn Security): And what about retention windows? We need 90 days for audit, but less for developer logs.
[05:21] Maya (Redwood AE): We can provide both. Storage retention can be configured; additional retention is an add-on. Logs can be redacted and stored with access controls; we'll include the security spec.
[05:34] Samira (Cairn): For benchmarking, we'll want to run our 95th percentile load profile. What's needed from our side?
[05:43] Liam (Redwood SE): We'll need a representative prompt set, concurrency profile (RPS over time), sample multi-step chat sessions (to measure KV cache behavior) and any attachment sizes for multimodal. Also your SLOs and cost targets.
[05:57] Jon (Cairn): Can Redwood run the benchmark in our VPC for realistic network egress? Our traffic patterns and routing matter.
[06:06] Priya (Redwood SE): Yes — benchmarks can run on Dedicated in your VPC or in Redwood-hosted Dedicated depending on your preference. Running in your VPC gives the cleanest picture for network latencies.
[06:18] Eli (Cairn): Any limitations on model variants or custom kernels? We prefer to run some fused kernels for our quantized models.
[06:26] Liam (Redwood SE): The serving runtime supports custom kernels in some environments; there are gating requirements for private/on-prem. For hosted Dedicated, we use our optimized kernel selection but can enable customer kernels with a compatibility review. We'll document the process.
[06:40] Samira (Cairn): Competitors question: we spoke to Vendor X (they did a deep infra sale) and Anthropic — what's your comparative advantage?
[06:50] Maya (Redwood AE): Redwood's focus is serving: predictable latency, unified ops across hosted/dedicated/private, and tooling for cost/perf tradeoffs. We aggressively optimize the runtime for batching and KV cache and expose controls in the Console. We can share benchmark references.
[07:07] Tanya (Cairn Security): Last security Q: SAML SSO + RBAC mapping must work with our existing IdP. Also need proof of SOC2 and pen test history.
[07:18] Priya (Redwood SE): We support SAML SSO, SCIM for provisioning, RBAC with custom roles. We'll attach SOC2 report and our pen-test summary.
[07:28] Eli (Cairn): Ok, next steps from our side: we'll share traffic percentiles, sample prompts, and a short list of critical routes. We'll also sketch a budget threshold for reserved spend.
[07:40] Maya (Redwood AE): Great. From Redwood we'll send the pricing/reservation options, security pack, and a benchmark plan. Proposal by end of next week.
[07:50] Samira (Cairn): One small nit — can we get an example of reserved sizing for our 95th percentile with and without KV caching? That helps justify reserved vs hosted.
[07:59] Liam (Redwood SE): We'll include a sensitivity table showing cost and latency with cache hit rates of 20/50/80%.
[08:08] Jon (Cairn): Will you also outline failure modes — e.g., if a reserved node preempts or a kernel fails — and the fallback options?
[08:16] Priya (Redwood SE): Yes — we'll include the failover plan: cross-region fallback, model variant fallback, and automatic throttling to protect SLOs.
[08:26] Maya (Redwood AE): Anything else?
[08:29] Eli (Cairn): No, feels good. Thanks everyone.
[08:33] Maya (Redwood AE): Awesome — we'll recap next steps in an email. Meeting adjourned.
